about: The free quota of each AI provider of AUTOMAT, as data (docs/MAINTENANCE.md, "The budget of the free quotas"). tools/ai-quota.py reads it; change a number here, never in code. Every number has its source. "verified": false means the number could not be checked against the provider's documentation on the day it was written: it is a conservative value (lower than what the provider is believed to allow), and the live rate-limit headers and 429 answers of each call correct the budget at run time. A person who checks a number against the provider's page sets it, with the date, and "verified": true. "source_verified_on" (2026-11-25) is the day a value was read on the provider's own page named in "source_urls": it is not a person's check, so "verified" stays false until a person sets it.

reserve.source: tools/ai-review.py asks two independent providers (three for a tier-B change) once each; one review is the diff, the failure and the checklist (MAX_DIFF, FAILURE_SHOWN, ANSWER_TOKENS), estimated here at 9,000 tokens

share_source: the owner's request of 2026-11-22 (one candidate cannot drain a provider), narrowed by the owner's decision of 2026-11-24 (no fixed share for real updates: they get all of the quota): the half holds only while ANOTHER security fix or real update is pending at the same time, so two real updates share a provider fairly; a lone one may use all of it

priority.about: The owner's decisions of 2026-11-24: "use the free AIs every day, always when needed, above all for real updates; what is left goes to self-evolution, drills etc.", and: real updates may always use ALL of every provider's free quota, at any time; background work uses only what real work leaves, and all of it. tools/ai-quota.py priority_of() puts every piece of AI work in one of four classes by its branch: 1 security fixes, 2 updates of what ships to users (everything not named below: the engine and ad-blocking crates, Brave's debounce list, uBlock Origin's scriptlets, the filter lists, Python and Qt, the Breeze icons, the daily candidate, a fix of main), 3 updates of the CI and the tools, 4 background work (the AUTOMAT drill, the replay bench, self-evolution). Classes 1 and 2 are limited by nothing but the providers' own quotas (security first in the order of the work; share_per_candidate only while two of them are pending at once). Classes 3 and 4 run only while no work of class 1 or 2 is pending or retrying (an open pull request whose latest checks are not green, or a row of failures in AUTOMAT's memory of the last pending_days days whose newest pull request was not closed after it; never a long-lived branch such as automation/autofix-main), never while that list could not be read (fail closed), and only in a provider's leftover window: the last release_hours hours before its own reset (the time below, verified or not); for a reset not verified also never during the real day's maintenance_window (UTC); then they may use everything left. Each provider's use is counted on its own day (the time and zone of its reset).
priority.drill_any_hour_about: TEMPORARY, the owner's decision of 2026-11-27: until this date the AUTOMAT drill may use the free quotas at any hour (not only in the leftover window), still never while a real update is pending; removed once the drill succeeds with the free AIs, and back to the rule of 2026-11-24 by itself after the date

maintenance_window.source: the real day's runs: security.yml 04:23, daily-check.yml 05:17, daily-maintenance.yml 06:17 UTC, then their tests and automatic fixes (several hours); until it is over the day's real needs are not known

priority.source: the owner's words of 2026-11-24; 3 hours, 2 days and the window are this repository's starting values, not the providers'

routing.source: a starting order only (strong: the agent that reads files and the largest context first; fast: the quickest answers first), unverified; tools/automat-route.py replaces it with the success rate AUTOMAT's memory records per provider and kind of task once a pair has min_samples attempts

Antigravity.what: Gemini's free tier, used by the Antigravity agent (one session reads and edits files in several requests) and by the reviewers through the Gemini API
Antigravity.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits (read on 2026-11-25): limits are per project, not per API key; no free-tier numbers are published for the text models any more ("can be viewed in Google AI Studio"). requests_per_day and session_requests stay this repository's own careful note of 2026-11-19; the others are careful guesses
Antigravity.signals_source: read on 2026-11-25. Google's own gemini-cli code (packages/core/src/utils/googleQuotaErrors.ts @08e9a20f, not Google's documentation): a QuotaFailure quotaId with PerDay or Daily, or 'limit: 0', is the day, read before a short retryDelay; PerMinute is a minute; a retryDelay over 300 s is the day (day_wait_seconds). The documentation lists no quotaId strings. The Interactions API (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/api-errors) names them: rate_limit_exceeded and too_many_requests (a minute, a burst), quota_exceeded ('exceeded your daily quota'). generateContent's 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED alone says only 'one of the API's rate limits (RPM, TPM, RPD, spend)' (aistudio.google.com/docs/api-errors.md)

reset.source: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits, read on 2026-11-25: "Requests per day (RPD) quotas reset at midnight Pacific time" (read on the provider's page, not checked by a person)

Groq.source: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits, read on 2026-11-25: the table gives openai/gpt-oss-120b, openai/gpt-oss-20b and qwen/qwen3.8-27b 30 requests and 8K tokens a minute, 1K requests and 200K tokens a day (the free plan's level: the models page gives the Developer plan 1K RPM and 250K TPM). Limits are per organisation; cached tokens do not count; some organisations also have input and output caps a minute. The organisation's own values: console.groq.com/settings/limits; read on the provider's page, not a person's check: conservative where the page gives no number
Groq.signals_source: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits, read on 2026-11-25: x-ratelimit-*-requests 'always refers to Requests Per Day (RPD)', x-ratelimit-*-tokens 'always refers to Tokens Per Minute (TPM)', retry-after (seconds) only on a 429, the other headers always. No header for RPM or TPD: only the 429's message, whose wording ('per minute (TPM)', 'per day (RPD)') is not shown on the official pages (not verified)

reset.source: console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits (2026-11-25) names no reset time: the headers give the time to the next reset ('2m59.56s'), which counts more; until a person checks it, the repository's own day (UTC) (read on the provider's page, not checked by a person)

Z.AI.source: docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, read on 2026-11-25: GLM-4.7-Flash and GLM-4.5-Flash are free (input, output, cached), GLM-4.7-Flash with 200K of context and 128K of output; no number of their limits is published (docs.z.ai/guides/overview/concept-param: the concurrency 'varies by user or plan'; the console's page needs a login): careful values; read on the provider's page, not a person's check: conservative where the page gives no number
Z.AI.words_source: docs.z.ai/api-reference/api-code, read on 2026-11-25. Z.AI answers every limit with HTTP 429 and a string error.code: 1302 'Rate limit reached for requests' and 1305 'temporarily overloaded' wait and are asked again (the deadlock of PR #111: they were taken as the day's quota); 1308, 1310 and 1314-1321 are usage limits that reset at their next_flush_time (hours or days), 1309 a plan expired, 1311 a model the plan does not include, 1313 the fair use policy: none is asked again today. 1113 asks for money (tools/autofix-reserve.py BILLING). 1303 is not on the official list. A "code:N" word matches only Z.AI's own "code" field, never a number anywhere in the text

reset.source: docs.z.ai could not be reached on 2026-11-24 and no reset time of its free models is recorded in this repository; the repository's own day (UTC)

error_codes.1113: 429 insufficient balance or no resource package (money: never asked again)
error_codes.1310: 429 weekly or monthly limit until next_flush_time
error_codes.1311: 429 the plan does not include this model
error_codes.1314-1321: 429 enterprise package or 5-hour / 7-day usage limits until next_flush_time

OpenRouter.source: openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits, read on 2026-11-25: free models, credits bought ever 'Less than 10': 20 requests a minute and 50 a day ('At least 10': 1,000 a day), one limit for the account whatever the keys; failed requests count; a negative balance blocks free models too; read on the provider's page, not a person's check: conservative where the page gives no number
OpenRouter.model_words_source: openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/llm-api-rate-limits (2026-11-11, not in the reference: not verified): a free model busy at its upstream provider answers 429 "temporarily rate-limited upstream" (limit_source upstream_provider_shared_pool); that is the model's own pool, shared by every free user, not the account's limit: the next free model is asked at once. Run 45625320020 (2026-11-25) waited 61 s on such 429s model after model; its log did not show their text, which the reserve prints since
OpenRouter.signals_source: read on 2026-11-25. The documented 429 body is {"error": {"code": 429, "metadata": {"error_type": "rate_limit_exceeded"}}} for a minute and a day alike (openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits), so that type says nothing of which. error.metadata.limit_source (openrouter_free_tier_per_minute, upstream_provider_shared_pool, openrouter_free_tier_daily) and the messages free-models-per-min / free-models-per-day are shown only on OpenRouter's blog (openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/llm-api-rate-limits, 2026-11-11), not in its reference: not verified. A 404 'No endpoints found matching your data policy' is the account's privacy setting (openrouter.ai/docs/faq), never a quota

reset.source: openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits, read on 2026-11-25: GET /api/v1/key gives free_model_daily_requests {used, limit, remaining} for 'the current UTC day'; OpenRouter's own OpenAPI spec: 'the counter resets at UTC midnight' (read on the provider's page, not checked by a person)

account.source: openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits, read on 2026-11-25: 50 free requests a day for an account that bought less than 10 credits ever (1,000 from 10). tools/ai-quota.py reads only is_free_tier (whether credits were ever bought) of GET /api/v1/key (tools/ai-providers.py OPENROUTER_KEY_INFO), with the key, at the start of each run that holds it, following no redirect: true confirms this value; anything else keeps it too, and the signing notice says the account is not on the free tier. The same answer has free_model_daily_requests {used, limit, remaining} for the current UTC day (documented, not read yet); rate_limit is deprecated, and money (limit, usage) is never read as requests. The count of the day comes from OpenRouter's 429s and their words

OpenRouter.headers_source: openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits, read on 2026-11-25: 'Successful inference responses do not include X-RateLimit-* headers'; a 429 of OpenRouter's own free-model limit carries X-RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset (Unix milliseconds), also inside error.metadata.headers. OpenRouter's blog (2026-11-11) shows them for the limiter of a minute (Limit 20), so they are read as a minute's; the day is read from the 429's words
